risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: Eight SAIRNfreedom resources in api/sd-data.js were readable and writable with a bare licence key and no session check: sf_operators (name + DOB + a FELONY flag and a GAMBLING disqualification flag on one row -- a criminal-history assertion about a named volunteer), sf_youth_participants (MINORS), sf_gaming_expenses and sf_disbursements (payee name + amount, the records ORC 2915.10(A)(2) and (C) require a charitable-gaming licensee to keep), sf_donations (donor name + amount), sf_staff (DOB, which the app age-gates off), sf_waivers (health and military-status disclosure) and sf_service_appointments (a member tied to a VA-adjacent referral outcome). The licence key is a bearer credential shipped to the browser. REPRODUCED LIVE WITH A CONTROL before the fix: on SF-PINNACLE-2026 with no session token all eight answered 200, while sf_ledger -- gated since 2026-09-21, same dispatcher, identical treatment -- answered 403 FORBIDDEN, so the difference is the gate and not an absent table. STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: every one returned ZERO ROWS on that tenant, so this shows nothing stops a caller REACHING the resource rather than that regulated data left. THE DISTINCTIVE PART IS NOT THE MISSING GATE, IT IS WHY IT STAYED MISSING: the dispatcher recorded the remaining 32 resources as a deliberate open product decision, and described them as a question about who may see -- quote -- a duty roster or a bottle count. That description does not cover minors, a felony flag or an ORC 2915 payee. The deferral was legitimate; it was taken against an understated description of the set, so anyone reading that line to decide was deciding about the wrong thing.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: sf_donor_awards and sf_members were reachable for read AND write on the SAIRNfreedom licence key alone, with no employee session. sf_donor_awards rows are {donorKey, tierId, state, updated} -- the donorKey identifies a donor and tierId resolves through sf_donor_tiers to a giving amount, so the row asserts THIS NAMED PERSON GAVE AT LEAST THIS MUCH. That is the same disclosure sf_donations was gated for on 2026-09-22, on the stated ground that donor identity is not public by default; gating donations and leaving awards open left the same fact reachable through a second door. sf_members carries member identity and the gate's own comment already named it an acknowledged gap rather than a decision. The licence key is a BEARER CREDENTIAL shipped to the browser, so it was the entire boundary on both.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: sf_signatures reached api/sd-data.js with no session gate: the SF_RESOURCES read and write branches dispatched on the licence hash alone, and the licence key is shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open the app. The row is {docId, docTitle, version, hash, signer, typed, signed} -- a named person, their typed signature, and the governance document it binds them to, with a hash of the text they signed. It is not a fact ABOUT a person but a reusable instrument that can be lifted off one document and re-applied to another, which is why it is sharper than the identity rows gated beside it. Named alongside sf_members in the 2026-09-22 finding; sf_members was closed that day and this one was left with the words 'the open-work row stays open'. Reachability was demonstrated live on 2026-09-22 -- 200 provisioned:true with no session token, against a control where sf_ledger answered 403 -- and exfiltration was NOT: every probe returned zero rows on that tenant.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: Four Tier A SAIRNfreedom resources -- sf_sessions (prizeCap, a statutory ORC Chapter 2915 limit, plus receipts and prizes), sf_shifts (a cash variance attributed to a named employee), sf_tickets (unitPrice and total at point of sale) and sf_rentals (charge, proceeds and the alcohol/notified compliance pair) -- were in neither SD_SESSION_GATED nor SD_GATE_APP, so the browser-shipped licence key was the whole authorisation on the gaming floor's money records; and in the same file sfHydrateAll() ran once from DOMContentLoaded BEFORE any interactive sign-in with sfEnterApp() never re-running it, so on a fresh browser every GATED sf_ resource's hydrate answered 403, the per-resource empty catch swallowed it, and signing in never went back for the server's copy -- already live for the 18 resources gated before this change

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: batch b18: SQL-SYNC finding, not a security gap. Michael's live-DB query (relayed via chat, this role has no Supabase credential) confirms rf_schedule's 3 new columns (status_changed_at, status_changed_by, status_changed_by_role) exist in the LIVE database. Direct repo read, this batch: grep -rn 'status_changed_by|status_changed_role|status_changed_at|status_changed_by_role' sql/ returns ZERO hits anywhere in sql/ -- no committed DDL file declares any of the 3 columns. This settles a b17 H1/H2 disagreement: H1's routing doc said 'confirmed present in sql/', this role's grep found none; both were partially right about different layers -- the columns are real and live, the repo's own tracked schema just never got the matching migration committed back. Independently found by H1 the same batch (logged H1 seq1348, same shape as H1's seq1345/1347 sairncode/stonedesk DDL-sync findings). Risk: a fresh provision from the repo's own sql/ files would NOT create these columns -- a real repo-vs-production sync gap, separate from whether the live run itself succeeded. Routed to hank: add the 3-column migration to the appropriate rf_schedule DDL file in sql/.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnroofing) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnroofing's photo requirement did not actually refuse, record ids were minted client-side rather than server-verified, and material that was UNAVAILABLE still counted toward a met threshold -- so a claim could present as fully evidenced on photos that were never required, ids the server never issued, and stock that was not there. rf_claim_photos is Tier A.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnroofing) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/rf-auth.js built MANAGEMENT_ROLES and BROAD_READ_ROLES as plain object literals, so every key on Object.prototype indexed truthy: seesAllRows({role:'constructor'}) returned true, reproduced live. A session carrying an inherited name passed the role half of every SAIRNroofing gate -- seesAllRows, ownsRow, and the ~40 sites in api/sd-data.js that index those maps directly -- granting cross-assignee read and write on rf_claims and rf_claim_photos, both Tier A. It was inert only because a SEPARATE array-based allowlist at provisioning (RF_ROLES.indexOf) refuses an unknown role, which is distant code the gate was silently depending on rather than a property of the check itself. Second defect in the same finding: the rf_claims write branch never stripped the caller's own assigned_employee_id from the stored data blob, inert only because the read branch's Object.assign happens to overlay the real column last.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnroofing) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/sd-data.js's rf_buildings write handler upserted EVERY optional column on EVERY write, deriving each from a payload field the caller may not have sent: location_id as trim-or-null, `active` as `payload.active !== false` (absent resolves TRUE), notes and data likewise. The one live caller -- saveBuilding() in sairnroofing.html:4650 -- sends only {building_id, name, customer, address}, so RENAMING A BUILDING from the app silently overwrote its server-side location_id with null, detaching it from the location -> entity chain the capital forecast attributes roof sections through -- and the same rename silently REACTIVATED a deactivated building. Found by H1 (log #536) while reading the register row, whose evidence cell asserted the opposite ("the app cannot set it wrong" -- true only of the UI form) and cited api/sd-data.js:7164, a line number that had drifted 216 lines to the rf_bonding write. Fixed by omitting absent payload keys from the upsert body -- PostgREST merge-duplicates only updates the columns present in the posted row, so absent means leave-alone while a present value, including an explicit empty string, still writes. Driven three ways: the shipped rename payload posts a body carrying neither location_id nor active nor notes; an explicit assignment writes LOC-9/false; an explicit empty writes null. The register cell is corrected in the same commit, citation re-anchored to the construct rather than a line number.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnroofing) has this defect on record
risks.risk: SIX CLIENT SAVE SITES STORED MODEL OUTPUT WITH NO PROVENANCE FIELD, AND THE SERVER COULD NOT KNOW. api/_lib/ai-safeguards.js landed in b9 with its own honest limit stated out loud: `ai_source` is a CLAIM BY THE WRITER, so 'a client that does not stamp it gets no gate'. No production client stamped it on a high-risk resource, so the approval gate was reachable and never reached -- and no server test can detect that. H2 traced four sites (seq852): sairnmechanical saveDoc -> mech_docs, sairnroofing saveMeasurementReading -> rf_photos, sairngrounds grdUploadProgressPhoto and sairnscape scpUploadProgressPhoto. rf_photos is the one that was not merely unlabelled: it is in HIGH_RISK_AI because an insurance supplement is built on the model's read of a measurement photograph, so stamping it switches a real refusal on for the first time in production. Two more found in this batch: stonedesk's Review Request Generator put model-written SMS text in front of an operator with nothing saying so, and that text goes to a named customer under the shop's name; and msb_bottle_scans, whose exclusion from REDACTION (correct -- no model prose is stored) was being read as an exemption from DISCLOSURE (wrong -- brand_read is what a model read off a label and the row syncs to the server). 18 arms green from 10 passed / 7 failed / 1 unproven; ablated four ways.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnroofing) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnroofing.html referenced var(--bd) three times and defined it NOWHERE, so three border:1px solid var(--bd) declarations were invalid at computed-value time and the border was DROPPED -- not drawn in a fallback colour. TWO OF THE THREE ARE THE AGREEMENT AND JOB-BOARD SIGNATURE CANVASES, where that border is the only thing showing a customer where to sign. These were the last 3 of the 153 contrast and undefined-token findings b30 measured across the platform; the ratchet baseline goes 3 -> 0 and the platform now carries zero contrast debt.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnroofing) has this defect on record
risks.risk: tests/roofing_claim_gate_single_source.js, arm "each branch keeps its own not-provisioned policy", ASSERTED SOMETHING IT NEVER TESTED. It said "the photo WRITE no longer refuses loudly" and tested /NOT_PROVISIONED/ inside src.slice(i).slice(0, 1400) -- A FIXED 1400-CHARACTER WINDOW. The rf_claim_photos write branch is 5,470 characters, so the literal that satisfied the window was the one in the CLAIM-EXISTENCE guard at the top of the branch, NOT the photo write's own refusal 34 lines further down at :9850/:9854/:9871. ROUTING THAT FIRST GUARD THROUGH THE SHIPPED notProvisioned() HELPER -- behaviour identical, literal gone -- TURNED THE ARM RED WHILE THE POLICY IT NAMES WAS FULLY INTACT AT THREE SITES. So for seven weeks a green arm meant "some occurrence of this string is within 1400 characters of the branch start", which is not the claim in its name and is not a claim anybody would make. SEVERITY MODERATE, reasoning stated rather than implied: no shipped behaviour was ever wrong, and the cost is that the arm guarding a Tier A claim-photo refusal could not have noticed that refusal being removed -- a false NEGATIVE in a guard, not a false claim to a user. REPAIRED: both halves sliced by BALANCED BRACE with an explicit overrun assertion; the test is on the POLICY rather than one spelling of it (the literal OR a notProvisioned()/notProvisionedText() call); and the arm's ACTUAL subject is asserted for the first time -- that the read's degrade-to-empty-list literal does NOT appear in the write branch, because the two policies differing is the whole point of the arm and was never checked. THE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS A REPAIR RATHER THAN A LOOSENING FITTED TO THE CHANGE: the repaired suite was copied into a HEAD~1 worktree and passes 23/23 against the UNCONVERTED handler too. FOUND BY A DIFFERENTIAL, NOT BY REVIEW: 230 suites referencing api/sd-data.js driven ALONE at HEAD and at HEAD~1; four came back red-and-unregistered and this was the ONLY one green at baseline. The other three were already red and are now registered in docs/known-red-suites.json. Full account: docs/2026-10-19-cody-b26-four-tier-reads-and-guard-conversion.md section 2.9.
